reference:
One day in June, the mountain had a visitor—a tall woman named Detie.
Along with Detie was her five-year-old niece, a girl with black curly hair named
Heidi.
"You are right. This is Heidi, the girl my late sister left behind," Detie
answered. "I'm taking her to Uncle Alp so he can take care of her from now
on."
But Detie had made up her mind. "It is time for Heidi's grandfather to take
up the responsibility."
Barbie had heard many tales about Uncle Alp, a grumpy old man who
hadn't been to church for many years, behaved with bad manners and scared
people off with his horrifying expressions. She was anxious to find out what
matter was with him.
Detie continued. "Tobias married my sister Adelheid, and Heidi was born.
But alas, Tobias died only after two years in a construction project, and poor
Adelheid passed away not long after, out of grief."
Finally, they reached Uncle Alp's hut, which overlooked the valley
Uncle Alp was sitting outside on a wooden seat when Heidi ran to him.
"Hi, Grandpa!" Heidi shouted out.
Uncle Alp was confused, until Detie explained everything to him.
And then, without listening to any
more of the old grumpy man's words, Detie waved goodbye to Heidi and quickly
went downhill.
